Sourdough starter, day 14

Posted 8 January 2024

Two weeks in, the starter has settled into a rhythm I can actually predict: it doubles in about five hours at 24°C, peaks, and then falls back over the next three. That predictability matters more than raw activity, because it is what lets you time a bake around the rest of the day.

The change came when I switched from a 1:1:1 feed to 1:2:2. The larger flour ratio slows the whole cycle down, which sounds like a step backwards but produces a much less sour crumb and a starter that tolerates being ignored for an afternoon.

What I changed

  • Feed ratio: 1:2:2 by weight
  • Water: filtered, 28°C
  • Flour: 80% strong white, 20% wholemeal rye

Next week I want to try a stiff starter at 60% hydration and see whether the peak window widens further. If it does, the overnight bulk becomes far less of a gamble.
